Alexander the Great (born 356 
bce, Pella, Macedonia [northwest of Thessaloníki, Greece]—died June 13, 323 
bce, Babylon [near Al-Ḥillah, Iraq]) was the 
king of 
Macedonia (336–323 
bce), who overthrew the 
Persian empire, carried Macedonian arms to 
India, and laid the foundations for the 
Hellenistic world of territorial kingdoms. Already in his lifetime the subject of fabulous stories, he later became the hero of a 
full-scale legend 
bearing only the sketchiest resemblance to his historical career.
